nodes.label: Linux Arch install runbook five invariants
nodes.norm_label: linux arch install runbook five invariants
nodes.summary: Reused id, same claim. The session re-verified that the runbook's instructions were still correct after its own state table went stale: the five invariants, the extraction-not-AppImage rule, the setsid --fork relaunch, the three-layer blank proof, and the pkill and gh release download -R traps. Only the state table and rollback paths were two releases out of date.

nodes.label: AppImage-bundled WebKit renderer abort
nodes.norm_label: appimage bundled webkit renderer abort
nodes.summary: Reused id, same claim. The AppImage is a carrier only: this host never runs it, because its bundled WebKitGTK kills the renderer, so usr/bin/snipset-desktop is extracted from it and installed instead. The runbook is explicit that a 585 MB usr/lib/* extraction is never wanted either.

nodes.label: Prefer the system WebKit over the AppImage's bundled copy
nodes.norm_label: prefer system webkit over the appimage's bundled copy
nodes.summary: Reused id, same stated reason. The AppImage's own WebKitGTK kills the renderer on this host, so the runbook extracts the binary from the AppImage and never launches the AppImage. The installed binary was independently confirmed to carry RUNPATH $ORIGIN/../lib against libwebkit2gtk-4.1.so.0, i.e. the system WebKit.

nodes.label: The in-app Tauri updater replaces the installed ELF with the AppImage
nodes.norm_label: in-app tauri updater replaces the installed elf with the appimage
nodes.summary: Verified against the updater endpoint the app actually calls and against the frontend updater path: on Linux the Tauri updater does downloadAndInstall() then relaunch(), replacing current_exe with the downloaded artifact, and for this project that artifact is Snipset_<ver>_amd64.AppImage. A separate prepare_update() in updater_cmds.rs:169 still logs the hardcoded Windows phrase 'allow NSIS to kill the app', which is a no-op on the Linux path.

nodes.label: Letting the in-app updater run would destroy the extract-install invariant, the backup chain, and CLI parity
nodes.norm_label: letting the in-app updater run would destroy the extract install invariant, the backup chain, and cli parity
nodes.summary: Three consequences were stated rather than assumed: the 39 MB ELF at ~/.local/bin/snipset-desktop would be overwritten by the 216 MB AppImage and then relaunched with its own bundled WebKitGTK, producing a white window; no *.bak-* is created and the overwrite cannot be rolled back; and resources/cli/snipset is untouched, so the CLI returns to the exact drift the runbook's section 3 says must be prevented.

nodes.label: install-arch-user-local.sh with an explicit --install flag and a read-only --audit mode
nodes.norm_label: install arch user local sh with an explicit install flag and a read only audit mode
nodes.summary: A new scripts/install/install-arch-user-local.sh encodes the whole runbook as one command. --audit is read-only and exits 10 when already current; --install is required to write anything. Guarded exits are 2 for app-running or low memory, 3 for a missing release, and a digest mismatch is rejected; a corrupted cache is unrecoverable without the added --clobber. Five real bugs surfaced by running it rather than reading it, and a sandboxed downgrade to 0.6.853 produced a byte-identical binary to the existing host backup.

nodes.label: Requiring an explicit --install is what stops a bare run or a typo from swapping the binary
nodes.norm_label: requiring an explicit install is what stops a bare run or a typo from swapping the binary
nodes.summary: Stated as the reason for the flag split, and paired with the observation that the exit-10 already-current guard is the one that would have saved the session's own wasted work, which was a 216 MB download and an 800 MB extract to install a version already present.

nodes.label: A published release can carry the right version string and stale content
nodes.norm_label: a published release can carry the right version string and stale content
nodes.summary: The user reported missing features, not a missing version. linux-v0.6.854 had been built from commit f64cd05c5 with 16 later commits on origin/main, and probing the installed binary confirmed get_customer_support_overview, export_customer_support_report and CustomerSupportTrendChart were all absent while 0.6.854 was present. The version comes from the merged tauri.linux.conf.json, not from the code, so a correct version proves nothing about content.

nodes.label: A correct version string is not evidence that the code is current, so the binary is probed for post-release symbols
nodes.norm_label: a correct version string is not evidence that the code is current, so the binary is probed for post release symbols
nodes.summary: The install itself was verified flawless: digest matched, the binary was ELF rather than AppImage, resources were 13 files, and the CLI showed no drift. Because 0.6.854 was present in the binary but the post-release Customer Support symbols were not, the conclusion drawn was 'the version is right, the content is old' rather than an install fault, and a new release had to be cut.

nodes.label: bun install --frozen-lockfile as a dependency coherence gate across CI and deploy scripts
nodes.norm_label: bun install --frozen-lockfile as a dependency coherence gate across ci and deploy scripts
nodes.summary: Reused id, same claim, seen as a live build blocker this time. Commit 74e232a0f, a Dependabot npm bump, raised five dependencies in package.json without regenerating bun.lock, so every bun install --frozen-lockfile in the repo had been failing since, CI included. The build of 0.6.855 died on it and rolled back cleanly. Bisecting eight commits on the VPS pinned the culprit exactly: f64cd05c5, cba7aa647 and 92d358a3c passed, 74e232a0f failed. Regenerating with the pinned bun 1.4.0 rather than the local 1.4.2 gave a 14-insert/12-delete diff that was exactly the five bumps and nothing else.

nodes.label: Minisign signature fail-closed
nodes.norm_label: minisign signature fail closed
nodes.summary: Reused id, same claim on the Linux producer. scripts/build/deploy-linux-github.sh hard-refuses to publish a Linux release without a minisign signature. The operational wrinkle found here is that the key is not in /root/cloudflare/.env at all; it lives in a separate /root/cloudflare/tauri-signing.env that must be sourced or the run dies at step 8. The VPS was also 6 commits behind origin/main, so a git pull is required first.

nodes.label: The Snipset/<ver> HTTP User-Agent as the per-build version marker
nodes.norm_label: the snipset ver http user agent as the per build version marker
nodes.summary: Version detection in the install script. A broad semver regex over the binary reported 169.254.169, the EC2 metadata IP, and a PCRE variant produced 8.6.0, 14.2.0 and 23.1.0. The runbook's own 0\.6\.8[0-9]{2} pattern works but is version-family specific. The User-Agent string Snipset/0.6.854 was found to be unique and unambiguous per build and was adopted as primary, with the SESSION_START version in the app log as a cross-check.

nodes.label: CustomerSupportStatisticsTab's inline fieldStyle bypasses the app's shared .input class
nodes.norm_label: customersupportstatisticstab's inline fieldstyle bypasses the app's shared input class
nodes.summary: The new component defined const fieldStyle = { display: 'block', width: '100%', marginTop: 4 } and applied it to its select and input elements: three layout properties and no visual ones. The codebase has no global input{} rule, so bare elements render browser-default. The fix replaced all four sites with className="input", matching the eight other select elements in the app, and deleted the now-unused fieldStyle.

nodes.label: Without a class there is no app styling at all, because no global input or select rule exists
nodes.norm_label: without a class there is no app styling at all, because no global input or select rule exists
nodes.summary: What makes fields look right elsewhere in the app is the .input, .textarea rule at base.css:174, which this component never used. Two earlier conclusions were corrected along the way: a minified-CSS match on input{ was the tail of .input-variable-modal__input{, the other was .search-bar input{, and the only bare element selector in the whole stylesheet is select at theme.css:134, which supplies appearance and a chevron but no border, background or radius.

nodes.label: The publisher stages the mirror file itself because auto-commit only covers staged paths
nodes.norm_label: the publisher stages the mirror file itself because auto commit only covers staged paths
nodes.summary: Reused id, same claim. The CLI runs git -C <vault> add -- <destination> for the one file it wrote, stages only, and never commits or pushes. Tests proved exactly one porcelain entry after one publish and two after two, that git rev-parse --verify HEAD still fails afterwards, and that the index is byte-identical across an idempotent skip.

nodes.label: Staging is required because obsidian-git's autoCommitOnlyStaged would otherwise let the mirror rot
nodes.norm_label: staging is required because obsidian git's autocomm tonlystaged would otherwise let the mirror rot
nodes.summary: The reason is in the vault's own plugin config: .obsidian/plugins/obsidian-git/data.json sets autoCommitOnlyStaged to true, so without staging, obsidian-git never commits the mirror and the copy silently rots. Staging only; do not commit; do not push.

nodes.label: source_hash as 12 lowercase hex characters
nodes.norm_label: source_hash as 12 lowercase hex characters
nodes.summary: Reused id, same claim. source_hash is the sha256 prefix of length 12 of the source plan and is the only freshness signal the mirror carries. The CLI hashes the utf8-decoded string rather than the raw bytes specifically to match the transform module, because a file with invalid UTF-8 would otherwise hash differently and look permanently drifted; a test asserts the emitted value equals sha256(readFileSync(plan))[0..12] for a normal file.

nodes.label: SKIPPED-IDEMPOTENT as a literal sentinel on the no-write path
nodes.norm_label: skipped idempotent as a literal sentinel on the no write path
nodes.summary: Before writing, the destination's existing source_hash is compared with the source's; on a match the CLI prints the literal string SKIPPED-IDEMPOTENT, writes nothing, does not stage, and exits 0. The string is emitted on the skip path and echoed in the --dry-run no-write branch, and is asserted as a substring in two tests. Idempotency was proved with the destination mtime forced to a known past value, so an unchanged republish is a real observation rather than a same-millisecond coincidence.

nodes.label: The SKIPPED-IDEMPOTENT string is referenced by the master skill file and the trigger snippet, so it must appear exactly
nodes.norm_label: the skipped idempotent string is referenced by the master skill file and the trigger snippet, so it must appear exactly
nodes.summary: Stated as the reason the literal cannot be paraphrased or reformatted: the master skill file and the trigger snippet both match on that exact text, so an emoji, wording or placement change would break the contract with the other layers.

nodes.label: PLAN_PUBLISH_CONFIG as the registry config injection point
nodes.norm_label: plan_publish_config as the registry config injection point
nodes.summary: An interface gap in the section 3.2 contract, which lists no way to pass a configPath to loadRegistry(configPath?). The CLI reads PLAN_PUBLISH_CONFIG from the environment and falls back to the repository plans.publish.json. An env var was chosen over a --config flag so the documented argv surface stays exactly as specified. A related gap: indexPath is not derivable from destPathFor, so the CLI computes it from indexTemplate and always passes it, because T2's frontmatter merge omits the related property entirely rather than guessing when it is absent.

nodes.label: Protected vault paths refused via a resolved path.relative segment comparison
nodes.norm_label: protected vault paths refused via a resolved path relative segment comparison
nodes.summary: protectedReason() compares the resolved path.relative(vault, dest) segments against ['Satset', '90 - System/Legacy'] and refuses with a non-zero exit. Tested for both folders, for a 01 - Projects/{project}/../../../Satset traversal that path.join collapses into a real Satset/ path, and negatively for a project merely named Satset under 01 - Projects, which is not refused. Destinations resolving outside the vault are refused too.

nodes.label: The protected-path check compares the resolved absolute path rather than the string, so a crafted path cannot escape it
nodes.norm_label: the protected path check compares the resolved absolute path rather than the string, so a crafted path cannot escape it
nodes.summary: Stated as the reason for resolving rather than substring-matching: a destination template containing .. segments is collapsed by path.join into a path that really lands under Satset/ or 90 - System/Legacy/. A prefix string test would have passed that destination through. Satset/ and 90 - System/Legacy/ are both protected by the vault's own rules.

nodes.label: A vacuous RED pass anchored with an existsSync assertion so it cannot pass with the feature absent
nodes.norm_label: a vacuous red pass anchored with an existssync assertion so it cannot pass with the feature absent
nodes.summary: The RED run was 1 pass and 27 fail. The single pass was vacuous: the missing-mirror test asserted exit 1 plus nothing written, both trivially true when the CLI does not exist at all. An existsSync(CLI) assertion was added to anchor it, and a positive-control test was added so an empty-index assertion could not pass for the wrong reason. A test-assertion bug was also found and fixed rather than papered over: with stageInVault:false the mirror is correctly left untracked, so the correct assertion is on the index (diff --cached), not on porcelain being empty.
